A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including material moved or renumbered in v3.

before.justification: V2 reports original simulations of Bernoulli, Gaussian, and nonparametric poly-forest recovery, with SHD and precise recovery results in Figures 1–2 and Appendix H.

after.justification: V3 retains those simulations and adds original baseline comparisons and dimension-scaling results in Appendix I.

M1.justification: PC-tree, its orientation procedure, and the Bernoulli, Gaussian, and nonparametric CI tests remain unchanged. The new poly-tree theorem analyzes the existing procedure rather than introducing an algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three synthetic distribution families and poly-forest recovery task. V3's additional experiments use the existing nonparametric setting; the connected-poly-tree extension is theoretical.

E2.justification: V3 introduces the first reported head-to-head comparisons, evaluating GES and Chow–Liu against PC-tree for nonparametric data with d=60. V2 reports only PC-tree performance.

E3.justification: Appendix I adds a comparison design using d=60 and n=700, 1300, 2000, 2500, 3000, plus an evaluation varying n/log d from 300 to 550. The original simulation settings and SHD/PRR metrics are retained.

E4.justification: V3 adds a focused analysis testing whether recovery rates align across dimensions when sample size scales with log d. V2 shows convergence with increasing sample size but lacks this normalized scaling analysis.

E5.justification: The new baseline table reports parentheses labeled standard errors, whereas the retained Figure 1 uses standard-deviation bars. Both versions retain the original 50-replication statement; no explicit increase in runs or new seed policy is reported.

E6.justification: Appendix I adds comparative SHD results and PRR scaling results. At n=2000, the new comparison reports SHD 0.05 for PC-tree, 6.00 for GES, and 0.10 for Chow–Liu. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v2 scores. The original Figures 1–2 are unchanged.

T1.justification: V3 adds Theorem 4.3 and Appendix F, including a Bernoulli Markov-chain construction and KL-divergence/tree-faithfulness lemmas supporting log d/c² optimality for connected poly-trees. Definition 4 also replaces the explicit triplet-membership requirement in H0 or H1 with membership in P alongside Markov and strong tree-faithfulness conditions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's central claims, and conclusion retain the same minimax reduction, distributional examples, PC-tree optimality, and empirical consistency claims. Listing experiments as a third contribution promotes validation already claimed in v2.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations of baseline competitiveness and alignment under n/log d scaling. It also newly claims the nonparametric simulations require more samples; the unchanged Figure 2 and the differing signal strengths acknowledged in Appendix I do not substantiate that cross-distribution interpretation.

D1.justification: V3 removes v2 Appendix H's replication-code availability statement and hyperlink. The data-generation recipes, thresholds, permutation count, CPU disclosure, and external UCI implementation link remain documented.

R1.justification: V3 adds Daskalakis et al. (2025), expands the contrast with Gaussian-specific results such as Wang et al. (2024), and removes the assertion that Jamshidi et al.'s CI test achieves the parametric rate. Most research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 revises selected introductory and definitional passages, adds a main-text proof sketch, expands experimental discussion, and updates notation and affiliation information. The main section order and most existing exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: The unchanged Figure 2 moves from the appendix into Section 6 beside Figure 1. V3 adds two empirical tables in Appendix I and two calculation tables in Appendix F, while retaining the basic document layout.

improvement.justification: V3 adds a connected-tree theorem, useful baseline/scaling evidence, and clearer exposition. However, it removes replication-code access information, adds an interpretation unsupported by the unchanged Figure 2, and introduces an inconsistent m=4c equality in the new Lemma F.2 proof. These substantive gains and reliability/reproducibility losses prevent a confident judgment about the net change in overall quality.
